explanations.explanation: Edom it is, baker. The passage says Mount Hor sits "…near the border of the land of Edom…" (Numbers 20:23). So Edom is the land by that mountain. You nailed it, and I didn't even have to stamp it into your hand.

Moab is a real land, friend, but it's not the one named here. The text says Mount Hor is "…near the border of the land of Edom…" (Numbers 20:23). So the neighbor is Edom. Moab is a fine guess, though, and I'd still pick you for my team.

Midian is another real place, but this passage doesn't mention it. It says Mount Hor is "…near the border of the land of Edom…" (Numbers 20:23). Edom is the land that goes with this mountain. Next time I'll hand you a little cookie map.

Careful, baker, this one flips it around. God says Aaron "…will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites…" (Numbers 20:24). The same verse says he "…will be gathered to his people…" So Aaron does not go in. I think that line lands heavy.

Right, baker. God says Aaron "…will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites…" (Numbers 20:24). The land is given to the Israelites, but Aaron won't walk into it. I think that's a heavy line.

That's it, baker. God says "…both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah." (Numbers 20:24). Notice God says both of them. He's talking to Moses and Aaron together. That's the reason He gives for Aaron not entering the land.

Nope, nobody runs away in this verse. God says "…both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah." (Numbers 20:24). The word is rebelled, and the command is God's. Running from the people isn't the charge here.

Good guess, but the text doesn't say anything about thanks. God says "…both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah." (Numbers 20:24). That's the charge, in His own words. It was about a command, not a thank-you note.

Eleazar, baker! God says, "Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor." (Numbers 20:25). Eleazar is the one who goes up the mountain with them. And hang onto that name, because the next verse says what Eleazar will wear.

Ithamar is another of Aaron's sons (Exodus 6:23), so that was a smart guess. But God names a different one here: "Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor." (Numbers 20:25). Eleazar is the name God gives for this climb.

Nadab is one of Aaron's sons too (Exodus 6:23), so you're in the right family. But the passage says, "Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor." (Numbers 20:25). Eleazar is the name God gives. It's easy to mix up a big family, and I only ever had to keep track of six cutters.

Yes, baker. God says, "Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar." (Numbers 20:26). The garments go from Aaron to Eleazar. It's like handing over the apron, and I'll tell you, mine has seen some flour.

A staff is a good guess, baker, but it's not what this verse says. God says, "Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar." (Numbers 20:26). It's clothing that gets moved, not something Aaron carries. Garments are what Aaron wore as priest, and they go straight onto his son.

No ring in this passage, baker. God says, "Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar." (Numbers 20:26). It's the garments that get moved over. Those are the clothes Aaron wore as priest.

True, baker. The text says they climbed Mount Hor "…in the sight of the whole congregation." (Numbers 20:27). So the whole congregation is in a position to see the three of them go up. That's a lot of eyes on one mountain, and I get nervous when two people watch me stamp.

Not quite, friend. The passage says Moses did as the LORD commanded, "…and they climbed Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation." (Numbers 20:27). So the whole congregation could see them. Nothing about this climb is hidden.
That's right, baker. "Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain." (Numbers 20:28). Three went up and two come down. I think that's a quiet walk, and I'll leave it quiet.

Close, but he's not alone. The text says, "Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain." (Numbers 20:28). Eleazar went up with him and comes back down with him. Now he's wearing Aaron's garments, too.

Joshua is a name you may know, so I see why you went there. He's the one who served Moses (Numbers 11:28), but he isn't mentioned in this passage. It says, "Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain." (Numbers 20:28). Eleazar is the one who made the climb.

Yes, baker. The text says "…the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days." (Numbers 20:29). That's the whole house of Israel, not just a few people. They mourn him for thirty days, and that's a real stretch of time. I think that tells us Aaron mattered to them.

That's not what the text says here. It says, "…the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days." (Numbers 20:29). They stay with their grief for those days. Nothing in this verse says they pack up and go.
No festival here, friend. The text says, "…the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days." (Numbers 20:29). They grieve him, all of them together. It's a quiet ending to a heavy passage.
